## 3. The evidence that moved it







**A randomised controlled trial of a large language model, in October 2024.**
[39009780](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39009780/) (*Nat Med*): outpatient reception via collaboration between
nurses and an LLM, randomised. This corpus spent 2025 recording the absence of
randomised clinical evidence for language models and building arguments on that
absence. The absence was not real.

**Pathology foundation models reach *Nature*.** [39232164](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39232164/): a pathology
foundation model for cancer diagnosis and prognosis prediction. With
[39039250](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39039250/) (*Nat Med*, clinical-grade computational pathology and rare-cancer
detection), the imaging branch of the foundation-model thread is publishing in
the highest-tier venues a full year before the single-cell branch attracts the
same attention.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

[39465898](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39465898/) (*NEJM*): large language models and the **degradation of the
medical record**. The harm is located in the clinical artefact rather than in
model accuracy — a different axis from every benchmark result, and the axis that
survives a model getting better. Filed as a refutation on `foundation-models`
because the thread's claim is about transfer into clinical use, and this says the
transfer damages the substrate.

### (b) Method credibility

Neither of this month's two AI-methods papers is a credibility result, and both
are here as notes rather than as ledger entries.

[39333790](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39333790/) (*Nat Comput Sci*) is STAMP, which splits genetic-perturbation
prediction into three ordered subtasks — which genes change, in which direction,
by how much — and reports substantial improvement over existing approaches on
single perturbations, multiple perturbations and transfer across cell lines,
along with the ability to recover regulatory genes and interaction types from
small samples. An improvement with no adverse finding attached.

[39443777](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39443777/) (*Nature*) is SynthID-Text, a production text watermarking
scheme that modifies only the sampling procedure, detects without running the
model, and was assessed over nearly 20 million live Gemini responses with no
measured loss of quality. Provenance infrastructure, which is what a field builds
when it expects not to be able to tell machine output from human output by
inspection — but a tool for establishing where text came from says nothing about
whether published methods are reliable.

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-27"
    Both entries overreached, in opposite directions. STAMP was carded `refutes`
    as an audit and read as evidence that "the task is already being rebuilt
    around its own weaknesses — the benchmark's authors had the objection before
    the null result was published", tied to a June 2025 result about simple
    controls. The word "benchmarking" in the title is the only thing in the paper
    that attaches to; the narrative was supplied by a reader who knew what 2025
    would say. And the watermarking paper was the single `supports` card among
    151 on `method-credibility`, carrying that thread's claim that published
    methods and reagents are reliable enough to build on without re-checking —
    which it neither states nor contradicts. Its stance alone moved the thread's
    supports count off zero. Both cards are now `neutral`, and STAMP has lost
    `method-credibility`.
